digests.title: TLDR AI — 2026-10-29
digests.tagline: Gemini 4 Carbon 🌱, Nemotron Transcribe 📝, benchmarker’s dilemma ❓

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google has introduced the Gemini 4 Carbon model, advancing AI capabilities with improved energy efficiency. This model enhances performance in natural language processing tasks while reducing carbon footprint, addressing sustainability concerns in AI development. Gemini 4 Carbon aims to set new industry standards for eco-friendly AI models.

stories.headline: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight model for multilingual transcription, translation, speaker attribution, and audio Q&A. It's ranked first across several transcription and speaker attribution leaderboards, supporting up to 40 languages with low error rates. Granary v2 enhances this by offering reusable data pipelines and fine-tuning options, enabling customization for diverse vocabularies and specialized applications.

stories.headline: Building an Inference Stack That Improves Itself (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: Decagon's AutoResearch agents diagnose inference bottlenecks, test optimizations against production traffic replays, and preserve findings across experiments. The company reports throughput gains up to 2.5x within endpoint latency requirements through quantization, scheduling, engine patches, and speculative decoding, with production changes requiring human approval.

stories.headline: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: Independent evaluation of language models is a hard task. It is difficult to create a number that is representative of current models that matches vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward-looking enough so that it's not outdated in three months. Independent evaluators dictate the winners and losers of a trillion-dollar market. They can also influence the direction of model development, increasing the pressure.

stories.headline: Qwenputer: a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5 (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Qwenputer is a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU that runs inside Qwen3.5. The CPU runs on its own Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM. It can run arithmetic operations and C and MicroPython code without any external runtime or tool usage. This post explains how the model works, how the model uses GDN layers as RAM, and how the developer also slotted in an experimental in-model file storage.

stories.headline: Introducing Vercel CI (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Vercel AI is now available in beta. The CI is able to keep up with coding agents. It runs only the tasks affected by a code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need. At Vercel, the system has decreased the time from git push to 'CI pass' by 2-6x.

stories.headline: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: GitHub Copilot Fusion lets Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate models for each task. It leverages the benefits of Project HydraFusion's multi-model orchestration and Copilot auto model selection's fine-tuned model selection to balance performance and cost efficiency. Copilot Fusion determines which models to use and how they work together depending on the level of effort selected by the user. Administrators can control which models Copilot Fusion can use and whether Copilot Fusion is the default.

stories.headline: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. It is now available through Microsoft Foundry. The harness gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. It was built to perform across model families, and is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service.

stories.headline: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic has launched reporting tools to help companies measure and optimize their AI spending with its products like Claude Code. The tools offer detailed insights on productivity, costs, and recommendations, addressing a major concern for enterprise clients. Despite competition from models like OpenAI's Astra, Anthropic's strong enterprise presence and sticky workflows continue to drive significant adoption and spending growth.

stories.headline: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta launched Waddle World, a virtual AI pet app that functions like a Tamagotchi, in the Philippines on iOS and Android. Unlike traditional productivity tools or chatbots, it serves as a digital pet and personal journal, allowing users to interact and play mini-games without pressure. The app reflects Meta's cautious approach following legal issues faced by other AI companion apps.

stories.headline: Build and manage Connected Apps in one place (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google has introduced a centralized platform for building and managing connected apps.

stories.headline: ElevenLabs Cue: Character-level audio timing (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: ElevenLabs' Cue is a forced alignment model for precise character-level timing in audio files.

stories.headline: Mirendil Introduces Lor for AI Research Automation (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Lor is a system with agents that write code, run experiments, and iterate for days across hundreds of parallel workers.

stories.headline: OpenAI now lets you text your Dot agent (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI now allows US Pro users to text their Dot agents via iMessage and RCS, enabling instructions through text, photos, and voice memos.

stories.headline: Copilot Automations now learn from outcomes and self-improve (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Copilot Automations now self-improve by learning from real-world outcomes on GitHub.

digests.title: TLDR IT — 2026-10-29
digests.tagline: Microsoft’s $33B Cloud Boom ☁️, OpenAI Eyes Google’s AI Chips 🔥, Claude Uncovers Critical Security Flaws 🐛

stories.headline: Google and Oracle are partnering to bring Google TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google Cloud and Oracle are partnering to bring Google Tensor Processing Units to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, making OCI the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs. The companies plan to deploy TPU capacity on OCI starting in 2027 to help organizations scale AI workloads across data centers engineered for AI density.

stories.headline: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reports (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI reportedly plans to purchase Google's Tensor Processing Units, expanding beyond its existing chip-rental arrangement. The potential deal would give OpenAI another source of AI computing capacity alongside Nvidia GPUs and its custom-chip development efforts with Broadcom, while strengthening Google's position in the AI infrastructure market.

stories.headline: Microsoft beats quarterly cloud revenue estimates (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft's Azure cloud business reported $33.17 billion in quarterly revenue, growing 48% year over year and beating analyst expectations. Microsoft is now disclosing Azure revenue in dollars, providing greater visibility into its cloud performance as the company continues investing heavily in AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: What enterprises can learn from Anthropic's IPO prospectus about vendor dependency (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic's IPO prospectus reveals that nearly half of its sales are routed through cloud partners Amazon and Google, highlighting significant vendor dependency and concentration risk across the AI ecosystem. Industry experts advise enterprise CIOs to treat AI procurement as a resilience conversation by questioning supplier supply chains and ensuring data and workflow portability.

stories.headline: Information overload is harming enterprise productivity - here's how IT leaders can solve that (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: A Forrester study commissioned by Staffbase found that fragmented workplace communication is affecting employee productivity, with 48% of respondents reporting reduced efficiency and 44% citing more errors or missed deadlines. The findings suggest that consolidating information and connecting workplace applications could reduce unnecessary context switching.

stories.headline: NVIDIA and Oracle Expand NVIDIA Vera Rubin to Multi-Gigawatt Scale (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: NVIDIA and Oracle have announced plans to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Superclusters with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems to multi-gigawatt scale. The companies are also bringing NVIDIA Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin GPUs to OCI to support AI training, inference, and agentic workloads. OpenAI has also trained and served frontier models on OCI infrastructure powered by NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.

stories.headline: Snowflake and Oracle: Bringing the AI Data Cloud to OCI (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Snowflake and Oracle are expanding their partnership to bring Snowflake's AI Data Cloud natively to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure as a first-party offering. Planned as an integrated service purchased and billed directly through Oracle, Snowflake on OCI aims to connect enterprise data across Oracle applications and databases with other sources to support analytics and AI workflows.

stories.headline: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: GitHub has introduced a new Copilot app, Copilot Fusion, for automatically routing coding tasks across multiple AI models and agent workflows spanning repositories and development tools. GitHub also announced that Enterprise customers can access Copilot features without purchasing a separate subscription, with usage billed through AI credits.

stories.headline: Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic researchers used an internal research model to discover critical vulnerabilities and construct sophisticated multi-step exploit chains in widely used software, including browsers, mobile operating systems, and kernel networking stacks. The model identified issues such as remote code execution, sandbox escapes, and lock-screen bypasses, which were reported to affected vendors under coordinated vulnerability disclosure. Anthropic argues that AI-assisted vulnerability discovery could help defenders identify and patch security flaws before attackers exploit them.

stories.headline: Oracle Cloud Acceleron adds AI-assisting networking enhancements (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Oracle expanded its Acceleron networking platform with new capabilities for AI and high-performance computing workloads. Updates include RDMA connectivity for front-end compute, expanded NVMe block-storage options, and communication libraries designed to maintain distributed AI workloads when network paths fail.

stories.headline: Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is now available on Google Cloud (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: The specialized AI model serves as a high-level brain for robots across various physical embodiments, combining spatio-temporal video understanding, long-horizon planning, and agentic tool orchestration for enterprise production environments.

stories.headline: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft is reminding Entra ID administrators to prepare for the February 2027 retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication.

stories.headline: Tesco eyes open source VMware alternative amid long-running spat (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: A Tesco engineering job posting outlines plans to migrate the retailer's edge virtualization infrastructure from VMware to Proxmox, offering another example of an enterprise evaluating alternatives amid Broadcom's licensing changes.

digests.title: TLDR Web Dev — 2026-10-29
digests.tagline: Gemini Carbon 💎, ship less JavaScript 📦, what frameworks cost AI agents 🧮

stories.headline: Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Next.js 16.4 adds an agent skill that uses Turbopack's module graph to find unnecessary client JavaScript, including eager imports, duplicate dependencies, and missed tree shaking. Vercel reports removing or deferring nearly two megabytes of compressed JavaScript across pages in v0 and vercel.com, with snapshot comparisons to verify each change.

stories.headline: How to make postMessage type-safe in under 350 bytes (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: typed-channel defines message names and payloads once so TypeScript can check both sides of a worker, iframe, or event-bus boundary. The core plus postMessage transport is 341 bytes with Brotli compression, while a separate request API adds typed replies and cancellation that propagates to the handler.

stories.headline: Local-First Means Three Different Things (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Local-first can mean offline capability, fast optimistic interfaces, or user ownership of data, and those promises lead to different architectures. Hologram prioritizes responsive local interfaces and offline support while retaining a server to enforce permissions and business rules.

stories.headline: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: A benchmark asks Opus 5.5 to build the same Pokémon app across JavaScript frameworks, then measures cost, time, spec compliance, performance, and accessibility over repeated runs. Hono with htmx, Astro, and Nuxt are among the cheapest in this experiment, but substantial run-to-run variance and a mostly content-focused app limit how broadly the ranking applies.

stories.headline: Website migration costs are going to zero (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI agents could make technical website migrations nearly free by using the existing site as a baseline for differential tests of pages and publishing workflows. The prediction shifts the durable sources of lock-in toward contracts, procurement approvals, and agent memory, making portable requirements and decision logs more valuable.

stories.headline: Nuxt DevTools v4 (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Nuxt DevTools v4 moves onto the framework-agnostic Devframe and Vite DevTools foundations, allowing it to reuse the Vite and Vue tooling ecosystem. A transition shim supports legacy modules while their integrations migrate to the new Devframe APIs.

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon for sustained coding workflows and cybersecurity, reporting 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability discovery and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching. Access begins with selected cyber defenders and trusted Fairwind partners, with broader availability still to come. Announced introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

stories.headline: Introducing Vercel CI (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Vercel CI enters beta with Turborepo-based task selection and remote caching, running only work affected by a code change. Vercel reports two to six times faster push-to-passed-check times while reducing the need for separate CI workflow configuration.

stories.headline: The October inflection point for vibe game development (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Opus 5.5 has improved at generating 3D models, music, and gameplay that is fun to play. Simple instructions can produce working games. More ambitious projects still need playtesting and iteration to fix gameplay problems.

stories.headline: Our AI Agent Executed the Same Successful SQL Query 254 Times (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: During a model comparison at Funnel, an internal data agent repeatedly executed a successful SQL query instead of finishing its task. The failure illustrates why model swaps need whole-system evaluation, explicit tool contracts, and bounds on repeated behavior.

stories.headline: Why Is This Fingerprinting Script Creating Bioweapons? (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: A browser fingerprinting script hides alarming prompts and variable names intended to trip LLM safety filters and frustrate automated analysis. Underneath the anti-LLM obfuscation, it collects conventional browser and WebGL signals and includes a gated Node.js routine for gathering system information.

stories.headline: Ghostty 1.4 (Website)
stories.blurb: Ghostty 1.4 adds complete Kitty graphics support, scrollback compression, faster terminal processing, improved SSH integration, and security fixes.

stories.headline: Node.js 26.13.0 enters LTS (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Node.js 26 has entered Long Term Support as Lithium through April 2029.

stories.headline: Yavashark: a new embeddable JavaScript engine in Rust (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Yavashark is an embeddable Rust JavaScript engine that passes 82% of test262 and supports Temporal, Intl, and TypeScript execution through its CLI.

stories.headline: Denial of service in body-parser (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: A decompression error in affected body-parser versions can crash a server with one request.

digests.title: TLDR InfoSec — 2026-10-29
digests.tagline: UEFI server root flaw 💻, Sony 2.5M data breach 🌐, GPS spoof cargo theft 🚛

stories.headline: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: A 16-year-old buffer overflow in TianoCore EDK2's PXE Base Code driver (CVE-2026-97631, CVSS 9.5), the reference UEFI code behind most server firmware, allowed an attacker to send an oversized ICMP error during network boot and execute ring 0 code before Secure Boot and the TPM chain of trust loaded. An AMI pull request leaked the fix months ahead of a January coordinated disclosure, although exploitation required local network access and per-model address tuning. Defenders should request patched firmware from their UEFI vendors, disable PXE boot where feasible, and monitor network boot segments for anomalous ICMP traffic.

stories.headline: Sony ISP Subsidiary Data Breach Exposes 2.5M Customer Records (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Sony Network Communications disclosed that an unauthorized party accessed 2.5M records from its So-net member database, which supports its internet access service. The records included full names, phone numbers, email addresses, user IDs, dates of birth, gender, and Internet connection IDs. Additionally, it exposed 54K email addresses and account passwords from several email services.

stories.headline: Hackers Target US Election Commission, Forcing Online System Shutdown Days Before Midterms (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Federal Election Commission (FEC) reported an outage in its filing system due to a cyberattack. The outage does not impact voting, just how campaigns report new funds flowing in. The FEC has not released details on whether any data was compromised.

stories.headline: Not Only ARTEX: The Different Levels AI is Used in Attacks Targeting Japan (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: TrendAI examined three attacker infrastructures targeting Japan, documenting autonomous attacks, AI-assisted planning, and suspected AI-written tools. CyberStrikeAI coordinated 44 agents against at least 19 organizations. Another operator scanned 6,000 Japanese IPs and stole hundreds of thousands of records through default credentials. A third used recovered VPN credentials to enter corporate networks. Evidence came from exposed attacker files. Victim-side confirmation remains incomplete.

stories.headline: What are Security Logs? (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Logs are structured records of security events in formats such as JSON, CSV, Syslog, and Windows Event Logs. Security engineers need to apply transformations to event logs to normalize the various formats and fields, making the data uniform for correlation and composite detections.

stories.headline: How Anchorage Digital and Turnkey verify code with AWS Nitro Enclaves (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anchorage Digital and Turnkey ran the open-source VisualSign transaction parser inside AWS Nitro Enclaves, where each parsed result was signed with an ephemeral P-256 key and bundled with a Nitro attestation document whose PCRs wallets checked against reproducible builds. The design let wallets prove that unmodified, audited code decoded a transaction, removing blind trust in crypto transaction signing by providing verifiable attestation rather than relying solely on network identity or operator trust. The open-source awsnitroverifier Go library handles certificate-chain and PCR validation, which any organization can use to verify their services running in AWS Nitro.

stories.headline: Infisical (Product Launch)
stories.blurb: Infisical manages secrets, encryption keys, digital certificates, and privileged access across cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Its Agent Vault inserts credentials through a proxy, keeping them from AI agents.

stories.headline: Snort 3 (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Snort Intrusion Prevention System 3 features improvements and new features resulting in enhanced performance, faster processing, improved scalability for your network, and a range of 200+ plugins so users can create a custom setup for their network.

stories.headline: CREBench (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: CREBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM performance in cryptographic binary reverse engineering. CREBench evaluates models over algorithm identification, key (IV) extraction, wrapper-level code reimplementation, and flag recovery.

stories.headline: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Thieves have stolen over $100 million in data center equipment since June. They compromise freight accounts through malicious links, then bid on shipments using hijacked identities, and those with fake licenses get accomplices hired as drivers. Two thefts involved ramming security escorts' vehicles. One $10 million shipment disappeared after its tracking coordinates were apparently spoofed.

stories.headline: AI 'hacker' finds 4 severe bugs in popular industrial control software in under 4 hours (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Causal Security's Cipher found four EPICS Base vulnerabilities in three hours and 49 minutes. One critical integer overflow, rated CVSS 9.8, could enable remote code execution. Three high-severity flaws permit crashes, memory corruption, or information disclosure. Exploitation requires network access to vulnerable EPICS services. EPICS controls equipment including particle accelerators and fusion experiments.

stories.headline: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Skyw4lker targets US manufacturing, technology, and healthcare organizations through device code phishing. Password-protected contracts or proposals send victims through Google Sites into legitimate Microsoft authentication flows. Completing attacker-initiated authorization gives attackers Microsoft 365 tokens. ANY.RUN identified obfuscated JavaScript and a PHP backend tracking victim sessions, IP addresses, and geolocation, and the backend repeatedly polls for authentication completion.

stories.headline: UK to look at making software companies liable for cyber breaches (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: The UK's latest budget commits the government to consulting next year on where liability for cyber breaches should sit, its first formal step toward holding software vendors accountable for insecure products, alongside £154 million for AI-driven cyber defenses that includes a £70 million NCSC vulnerability exposure centre.

stories.headline: Bank of America kindly asks that you don't share your banking password with your AI assistant (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Bank of America emailed customers warning against sharing banking credentials with AI assistants or other outside services, as sharing credentials can expose accounts to unauthorized transactions, fraud-triggered lockouts, or password leaks through assistant vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: IR 8547, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: NIST finalized its roadmap for phasing out quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms in favor of its PQC standards, backing a June executive order that requires federal high-value systems to adopt PQC key establishment by 2030 and signatures by 2031.

digests.title: TLDR Design — 2026-10-29
digests.tagline: Genie 4 Worlds 🌍, Touchscreen MacBook 💻, Google Photos Redesign 📸

stories.headline: Google Photos Rolls Out a Customizable Redesign of Your ‘Collections' Tab (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google Photos on Android is getting a customizable Collections tab that lets users pin frequently opened collections, hide sections they rarely use, and rearrange the layout. Favorites, Screenshots, and Trash are pinned by default, while albums, people and pets, places, and other categories get carousels that can be hidden or reordered. The update arrives with Google Photos version 7.97 through a server-side switch, with no broader release date announced.

stories.headline: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro comes in 14- and 16-inch sizes, pairing a PROLED XDR display with a Dynamic Island-style cutout and a lighter body. A redesigned hinge keeps the screen steady during touch input, while M5 Pro and M5 Max chips power both models. Prices start at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model, with preorders opening October 30 and availability beginning November 6.

stories.headline: We're Announcing Genie 4, Our New World Model for Real-Time Interactive Simulation (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's Genie 4, a new world model for real-time interactive simulation, brings more realistic visuals and native audio to generated worlds. Natural-language prompts steer scenes live, from moving the camera to changing the weather or adding characters. Rollout starts with a limited group of trusted testers, with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early-access Gemini API partners coming soon.

stories.headline: Designing for People with ADHD (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: ADHD affects about 5% of people and stems from differences in how the brain develops focus, planning, and self-regulation. It is not a matter of willpower. Helpful patterns include reminders for unfinished drafts, chunked long forms, gradual disclosure of options, and visible progress, while autoplay and infinite scroll are best avoided. ADHD often overlaps with autism, dyslexia, and anxiety, so designing for it tends to help several groups at once.

stories.headline: A select should tell you something (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Customizable HTML selects can now include previews, secondary information, warnings, and other context that helps people recognize the right option instead of deciphering text labels. Practical examples include showing fonts in their actual typefaces, displaying current local times instead of UTC offsets, aligning delivery prices for comparison, and distinguishing people with identical names by job title and department. The technique progressively enhances the native `select`, so unsupported browsers can retain familiar controls while richer desktop experiences provide more useful information without replacing built-in semantics and keyboard behavior.

stories.headline: One size doesn't fit all: rethinking “good design” across cultures (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Ideas such as clarity, simplicity, restraint, and functionality are often treated as universal measures of good design even though they emerged from particular Western histories and cultural contexts. Design traditions excluded from the dominant canon can use decoration, complexity, symbolism, and craft in ways that are deeply functional within their cultures, challenging assumptions that minimalism is inherently more sophisticated or understandable. Evaluating design more broadly requires asking who established prevailing standards of taste, whose histories were documented and taught, and whether a design successfully serves its specific cultural purpose rather than conforming to a supposedly universal aesthetic.

stories.headline: Animated Architecture Diagrams from Plain Text (Website)
stories.blurb: Declare semantic nodes, flows, and timed beats in reviewable text. Markdy compiles browser-native motion graphics that stay version-controlled, PR-friendly, and AI-native.

stories.headline: Open-Source CAD for AI Agents (Website)
stories.blurb: The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL, or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks, generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal, and CNC fabrication services.

stories.headline: Make Wild Visual Effects in Your Browser (Website)
stories.blurb: Ladybug is an effects studio for pictures, video, type, and sound.

stories.headline: The New York Times turns 175 with an identity, events and a campaign (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: The New York Times is marking its 175th anniversary with a visual identity, campaign, and program of events that use the publication's history as material rather than simply commemorating its age. Familiar elements from its editorial and typographic heritage are reframed across contemporary applications, connecting decades of journalism with the publication's current cultural role. The system demonstrates how an established institution can celebrate recognizable brand equity while giving historical assets new relevance instead of replacing them.

stories.headline: The Software Factory Forgot About Design (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: A four-station workflow of Linear, Paper, a coding agent, and review brings design into the software factory, where issues otherwise turn straight into pull requests. Linear holds the intent, Paper hosts agent-drafted HTML and CSS designs made before implementation, and the coding agent builds from both issue and design. Review checks the build against intent, but agents still lack the history behind decisions, such as past designs, analytics, and design-system reasoning.

stories.headline: How Mother Design turned a séance into a new identity for Purple Garden (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Mother Design began Purple Garden's rebrand with a séance, chakra reading, and automatic drawing workshop, using the resulting forms and feelings to build an identity around spirituality as “A Living Practice.” A whimsical wordmark, crystal-like guidance glyph, warm purple palette, tactile imagery, living typography inspired by cymatic patterns, and expressive motion create an immersive system without relying on familiar psychic-industry clichés. The process moved between physical experimentation, traditional design software, and AI tools, deliberately introducing unpredictability into both the creative process and the finished identity.

stories.headline: This Creative Agency's Website is Giving Me Tumblr 2000s Vibes, and I'm Here for It (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Denver's Bound Agency has a handmade, scrapbook-style site by Wunder Werkz that evokes 2000s Tumblr, with a handwritten logo, doodled icons, and tarot cards.

stories.headline: struggle together (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI can remove much of the difficulty involved in learning and making things, but some of that struggle builds judgment, understanding, relationships, and the ability to create things with other people that none could have made alone.

stories.headline: Stefan Sagmeister's Artworks Turn Global Data into Good News at La Gaîté Lyrique (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Stefan Sagmeister's solo show "Finally, Something Good" at La Gaîté Lyrique turns UN and World Bank data into artworks arguing that health, democracy, and equality have improved.

digests.title: TLDR Data — 2026-10-29
digests.tagline: How Netflix Debugs with AI 🔍, Database Benchmark Battle 🏁, Privacy at the Access Point 🛂

stories.headline: The 2026 Cloud Data Warehouse Benchmark (Website)
stories.blurb: At 100 GB, MotherDuck led in single-user speed and cost (235 ms, $0.00124/query), Fabric served 100 concurrent users under five seconds for $5.76/hour, and ClickHouse failed 20.4% of single-user runs. Databricks had the smallest latency increase from 1 GB to 1 TB (3.7x versus MotherDuck's 30x), with tuning and autoscaling disabled throughout.

stories.headline: The paper that split the database in four: inside Azure SQL Database Hyperscale, aka Socrates (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Azure SQL once kept four full copies of each database, which capped practical size at around 4 TB. The 2019 Socrates paper separated the log from storage, so durability and availability could scale apart. This change in approach let Hyperscale reach 100 TB, halve storage copies, and restore a 50 TB database in minutes.

stories.headline: How JD.com Built a Lakestream with Apache Fluss and Apache Hudi (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: JD replaced parallel streaming and batch training-data pipelines with a staged migration: write once to Fluss, tier to Hudi, and union fresh plus historical reads. The difficult part is consistency: workers coordinate a single Hudi commit per tiering round and report matched stream offsets only after it completes. That pattern enables rollback-safe catch-up, but leaves schema evolution and dynamic bucketing unresolved.

stories.headline: Best Practices for Single Row Lookups (Point Queries) (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: DataFusion can perform surprisingly well on point lookups when tuned for retrieval instead of analytics. The biggest gains came from storage layout and execution choices that minimize unnecessary work, such as sorted Parquet files, right-sized row groups, metadata caching, and prepared statements. The broader lesson is that analytical engines can serve low-latency reads if the workload is designed deliberately.

stories.headline: Getting an analytics agent from 50% to 96% accuracy (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Benchouse improved nao's accuracy from 49.6% to 88.2% by switching from Sonnet to Opus, then reached 96.5% with better context. The key fixes clarified business metrics, removed ambiguous terminology, and told the agent to use agreed calculations before suggesting alternatives.

stories.headline: The Benchmarking Crisis (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI code generation is helping database engines game ClickBench. One, pgrust, groups strings by hash value alone, caches predicates the benchmark repeats, and on one query skips most of the data. Any benchmark stops being useful once systems optimise for it, and vibe-coded engines have no customers to keep them honest.

stories.headline: SLayer (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: SLayer is an MIT-licensed, embeddable semantic layer for governed agent and human access to warehouse data through MCP, REST, SQL, or Python. It combines read-only connectivity, SQL translation, transformations, row-level security, semantic search, and memory, and imports dbt, Cube, or Ossie definitions. Its expression model supports ratios, time shifts, and multi-stage queries beyond fixed BI metrics.

stories.headline: PrivacyLib: Privacy Controls at the Data Access Boundary (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta built PrivacyLib to enforce privacy rules at the moment data is accessed, replacing one-off integrations with shared controls that work across many systems. The key lesson is to normalize diverse data platforms into a small set of common operations, which makes policy enforcement reusable, scalable, and adaptable enough to extend from traditional infrastructure to AI agents.

stories.headline: Egres: A Postgres-compatible database for heavy, multi-tenant workloads (26 minute read)
stories.blurb: What would Postgres look like if designed today? Egres is the answer: a new open-source database that speaks the Postgres protocol but shares almost no Postgres code. It runs thousands of tenants in one process, metering CPU, memory, and disk per query, and its benchmark used 46% less disk than Postgres 18.

stories.headline: Gems of DuckDB 2.0.0 (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: DuckDB 2.0 adds a Python appender for batching generated rows, CLI function manuals and queryable command history, plus secure views that hide underlying statistics and query plans. Other additions include custom partition paths, sorting within exported partitions, direct GeoJSON exports, and support for extension-defined window functions.

stories.headline: DuckDB Universe (Tool)
stories.blurb: The DuckDB Universe is a searchable map of 516 open-source projects and 59 companies and products using DuckDB, spanning extensions, dashboards, libraries, and database integrations. Entries include GitHub star counts and source links, with examples ranging from PyGWalker and Evidence to MotherDuck and DeepSeek's smallpond.

stories.headline: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Netflix made failure diagnosis more reliable by using LLMs to identify the exact log spans behind an error and provide on-demand root-cause analysis, instead of asking models to digest entire logs. That design improved coverage to all failures while reducing hallucination risk and latency, and early usage data suggests it sharply cuts manual log exploration during debugging.

stories.headline: Reducing BigQuery Costs Through Its Biggest Problem: The Users (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: An open-source BigQuery FinOps agent cuts waste from user-written SQL by detecting common cost mistakes, rewriting queries, and validating savings before execution.

stories.headline: How Flink's Kafka connector commits offsets to Kafka (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Flink's Kafka connector now reconciles checkpoint state with Kafka's actual position, preventing misleading offsets on transactional topics and making its committed-offset metric match Kafka tooling without weakening exactly-once processing.
